reasons: The shapes are maintained by hand with no check against the backend.
Several fields are optional or loosely typed.

terms.meaning: A version of JavaScript that checks the shape of data before the app runs.
A named description of what fields a piece of data has.
A field that may be missing. The code marks these so the checker asks the code to handle a missing value.
The step where code is checked and converted before the app runs.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose note
sections.what: Opens the file with a note that these are the data shapes the frontend expects from the backend.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the frontend in step with the backend's data format.

sections.name: CostRange
sections.title: Cost range shape
sections.what: Describes a low and a high cost estimate, plus an optional middle value called the median.
sections.why: Likely reason: cost figures are given as ranges to show uncertainty.
sections.watch_out: The median is optional, so code that uses it must handle it being missing.

sections.name: ComponentCost
sections.title: Component cost shape
sections.what: Describes one cost part: its ranges for two price measures (MSP and MMP), a formula description, an optional breakdown by sub-part with percentages, and its unit.
sections.why: Likely reason: every cost part is reported the same way so the screens can show them alike.
sections.watch_out: The breakdown is optional, so the screen must check it exists before showing it. The full names of MSP and MMP are not given in this file.

sections.name: SystemInputs
sections.title: System size inputs shape
sections.what: The overall project settings: size in kilowatts, the DC to AC ratio, and an optional storage length in hours.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the top-level project choices.
sections.watch_out: Storage length is optional, so a missing value must be handled wherever it is read.

sections.name: ModuleInputs
sections.title: Module inputs shape
sections.what: Solar panel settings: efficiency, physical size and weight, yearly output capacity, labor hours, electricity use, depreciation, an upkeep rate, and low and high cost.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The fields are grouped so the input form can fill them together.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a field here without matching the backend leaves that input blank in the app.

sections.name: InverterInputs
sections.title: Inverter inputs shape
sections.what: Inverter settings: the type (central, string, or micro), yearly output capacity, low and high cost per kilowatt AC, labor hours, depreciation, and efficiency.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The type accepts only three exact names, so any other spelling will fail the type check.

sections.name: ESSInputs
sections.title: Storage inputs shape
sections.what: Battery storage settings: whether storage is on, then optional cost, project, incentive, efficiency, and cycle values.
sections.why: Likely reason: most storage fields only apply when storage is turned on, so they are optional.
sections.watch_out: Storage can be turned on while a value is missing, which can lead to blank results.

sections.name: SBOSInputs
sections.title: Mounting inputs shape
sections.what: Racking and mounting settings: area per kilowatt, whether trackers are used, and optional tracker and fixed-mount costs.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Tracker cost fields are optional, so they can be empty even when a tracker is used.

sections.name: EBOSInputs
sections.title: Electrical balance inputs shape
sections.what: Electrical settings: low and high costs for transformers, breakers, combiners, and wiring, plus shipping and tariff rates.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: LaborInputs
sections.title: Labor inputs shape
sections.what: Field and office labor settings: an hourly rate and hours per kilowatt for each, plus a labor burden rate.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: OtherCostsInputs
sections.title: Other costs inputs shape
sections.what: Rates for sales tax, contingency, management, and profit.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The code does not say whether these are fractions or whole percentages, so check which one the backend expects.

sections.name: OMInputs
sections.title: Operations and maintenance inputs shape
sections.what: Yearly low and high costs for cleaning, inspection, replacement, insurance, property tax, and lease, plus a discount rate.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The lecture step on operations covers a 20-year period.
sections.watch_out: The discount rate has the same fraction-or-percentage question as the other rates.

sections.name: CostModelInputs
sections.title: Combined inputs shape
sections.what: Groups all input sections into one object that describes the whole model.
sections.why: Likely reason: one object is sent to the backend with every choice in it.

sections.name: SystemTotal
sections.title: Overall total shape
sections.what: The overall project total: a cost range, a formula description, and a unit.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: CostModelOutputs
sections.title: Calculation results shape
sections.what: The results: one cost part for each area, two totals (with and without storage), a time stamp, and the session id.
sections.why: Likely reason: all results come back in one package so the screens read them from one place.
sections.watch_out: The storage result and its total are optional, so screens must handle them being absent.

sections.name: ValidationResult
sections.title: Input check result shape
sections.what: One check result for an input field: the field name, a status (valid, warning, or error), a message, a severity, and optional suggestions.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the form show clear feedback next to the field it concerns.
sections.watch_out: Status and severity are separate fields, so a screen that reads only one may misreport a problem.

sections.name: WebResearchSource
sections.title: Web source shape
sections.what: One web source used in research: title, link, short excerpt, a relevance score, and when it was found.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the citation details that the research panel shows.
sections.watch_out: The code does not state the range of the relevance score. The panel treats it as a value from 0 to 1 when showing a percentage.

sections.name: WebResearchResult
sections.title: Web research result shape
sections.what: The research for one cost part: input and output checks, suggestions, quotes, sources, and a confidence value.
sections.why: Likely reason: one package per component lets the research panel show each one.
sections.watch_out: The input and output checks are loosely typed, so the editor does not check their contents.

sections.name: CalculationStep
sections.title: Lecture step shape
sections.what: One lesson step: number, title, component, visual details, explanation, formula, example, sub-parts, context, and optional research.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the lecture steps the backend builds.
sections.watch_out: Research is optional on a step, so a step may have none attached.

sections.name: LectureSequence
sections.title: Lecture sequence shape
sections.what: The whole lecture: total steps, the list of steps, the current step number, and percent complete.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app show progress through the lecture.
sections.watch_out: Progress values come from the backend, so the screen should not assume they match the list length.

sections.name: ErrorDetail
sections.title: Error detail shape
sections.what: One error message: a code, a type, text, an optional field name, an optional suggested fix, and a severity of critical, error, or warning.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user specific problems to fix.

sections.name: ModelResponse
sections.title: Calculation reply shape
sections.what: The reply to a calculation request: a success flag, the results if any, check results, research, lecture steps, errors, warnings, and extra data.
sections.why: Likely reason: one reply shape lets the store handle every outcome the same way.
sections.watch_out: Results are missing when a calculation fails, so code must check the success flag before reading them.

sections.name: Session
sections.title: Saved session shape
sections.what: A saved session: id, creation time, last update time, and optional saved inputs, outputs, research, lecture, checks, and warnings.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a past run be reopened later.
sections.watch_out: Most saved fields are optional, so a session may open with some sections empty.

sections.name: SchematicComponent
sections.title: Diagram box shape
sections.what: Describes one box in a diagram: id, type, icon, position, layers with cost text and color, connections, and whether it is conditional.
sections.why: Likely reason: a diagram needs position and connection data for each box.
sections.watch_out: The cost here is text, not a number, so it is not added up automatically.

sections.name: SchematicVisualization
sections.title: Whole diagram shape
sections.what: Describes a whole diagram: its boxes, the active box, highlighted layers, and whether cost labels show.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Not used in the files shown here, so check where it is used before changing it.

sections.name: ChartDataPoint
sections.title: Chart point shape
sections.what: One point or bar for a chart: a name, optional low and high cost values, and a single value.
sections.why: Likely reason: charts need one shared shape for the ranges they draw.
sections.watch_out: Every value field is optional, so a chart point may be empty.

sections.name: WaterfallDataPoint
sections.title: Waterfall chart point shape
sections.what: One step in a waterfall chart: a name, a value, a running total, and whether it is an added amount or a total.
sections.why: Likely reason: a waterfall chart shows how costs build up to a total.
sections.watch_out: The running total must match the values, and this file does not enforce that.

summary: Defines the shapes of the data the frontend expects from the backend and uses internally, so the editor can catch misspelled or missing fields.
purpose: A single list of data shapes that the rest of the frontend shares.
why: Likely reason: the header says these mirror the backend schemas, so the two stay in step. Kept by hand.
how: It lists small building blocks first (cost ranges and component costs), then groups the input values by area: system, modules, inverters, storage, mounting, electrical balance, labor, other costs, and operations and maintenance. After that it lists outputs, research, lecture steps, sessions, errors, the reply shape, and the chart and diagram shapes.
inputs: Nothing is read at run time. The file is used only when the code is checked.
outputs: No output at run time. It supplies shapes to other files.
risks: The shapes are written by hand. If the backend renames a field, the frontend still compiles and may show blank values. Several research fields are loosely typed, so their contents are not checked.
debug: If a value is undefined in the app, compare its name here with the backend field name. These shapes are removed when the app runs, so they cannot show errors in the browser.
